questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I do taekwon-do, so I wanted to go to the motherland - Korea.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Taekwon-do

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I think in the moment that I thought that everything was very overwhelming... Remember, everyone wants to help you the best they can so everything will be alright if you do your best to follow along. Make sure that you attend the orientation and have read up on things and have found accommodation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation day and SKKU has a international office that I went to with some questions about courses and general everyday things about student life in Korea.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found housing at Simple Spaces Korea. They have some different ways of housing and I lived in the 10 person house in Yaksu. 
There is also Kim's Community. Both of these are marketing themselves towards expats or exchange students and have trips and activities planned outside of university. Great way to meet some people who are in the same boat as you. 
From what I've heard are the campus dorms fine - they are generally two people rooms, but they probably pair you up with another exchange student. You can't have visitors in the dorm and there is a curfew on weekdays.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I haven't heard anyone getting scammed about housing - there are appartment called gushiwons, where you have a room and share a kitchen with everyone in the appartment. The quality varies a lot from gushiwon to gushiwon so be on the look out for some nice ones, if you want to live in those. Personally, I would recommend Simple Spaces as I thought that they were nice and good at accommodating us in my house.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Fairly straight forward. Filled out the forms - transcripts, bank statements, passport and then they send you a participation agreement. I didn't think it was too difficult, but they are a bit slow to send it. I felt like everyone else who attended different universities in South Korea got there acceptance and forms before us...

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an email... Be patient though.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got up at 3 am to apply for the ones I wanted so I got them all. One of the professors asked us to drop one class because they didn't have enough space for their Korean students which kind of sucked. But I found another one when I got to SKKU.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to search through all the different campus' and degrees. It wasn't completely intituitive which classes I could take and some classes don't allow international student. Use the "language in international language" as a guide. However, many of the classes are still partially in Korean even though it is marked as "international language"...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I couldn't find enough relevant master courses so I took bachelor's courses. I had some trouble with a long waiting time for my pre-approval of courses because I was a masters student taking only bachelor's courses. However it worked out. Remember that it is UCPH's responsibility that you can take the courses that makes most sense for your education. Even if it takes a long time, if you have good reasons to take only bachelor's courses or a specific course, then write to Studenter service.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In SKKU, for natural sciences courses the style is way different than UCPH. It is basically, "here is a 1,5 hour presentation, remember everything." No practical exercises, no repetition other than if you do some yourself. Took me a bit of time to find a good way of studying and even then I was not as satisfied as at UCPH. However, don't stress too much about how well you are doing. The professors know that the life of an exchange student is different than native Koreans so probably they pull some punches. Just be sure to do your best and show up for the majority of the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biodatamining (GBE3071-41)
Genetics (IBT2003-41)
Trends in Computational Biology (IBB3017-41)
Intensive Korean (IKP)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Trends in Computational Biology (IBB3017-41), 
Balachandran is really nice and a good teacher. The only course where we got to do group work, which I missed in the other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: To get your visa there is a 420 dkk price tag and to get the ARC (alien registration card) after you have arrived there were some costs for taking a decent photograph. They also have a compulsory national health insurance (NHS) - if you have travel insurance at home (I made one with IDA) then you can get exempt. Do that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is really cheap, transportation as well. 
Groceries are really expensive basically like in DK but the quality is worse. Just eat out or at the convenience stores.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different clubs and activities. I didn't really attend any, but I heard that they were great fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club. I did taekwon-do outside of university, but joining any club is the best way to get in contact with locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out of Seoul. There are some really nice sights in South Korea. Do trips to Busan, Jeju Island and other smaller cities. Also visiting other countries in East/South-east Asia is really convenient when you are in South Korea already.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very difficult at first, however after the first month everything was running smoothly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: JOIN A CLUB!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No talk Korea bus

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very polite. I didn't feel gawked at or like I didn't belong. Most Koreans won't treat you that different.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get accommodation. Research which courses are available. Have patience and be ready to check your email everyday and to communicate if something needs to be clarified.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. Everything will work out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having Korean language class and doing taekwon-do on a higher level than at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my girlfriend, family and friends for such a long time...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You got this. Everything is going to be alright

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
